# The company and its market:
*Name and location:* QGS Solutions (based in Narbonne).

 *Sector and positioning:* Sector and positioning: Created in 2024, QGS Solutions is a company specializing in helping small businesses, SMEs, and self-employed people with their IT management and data security. QGS Solutions is an operating company in the competitive sector of IT services and local assistance.

*Internship framework:* Internship context: I have participated as a full-stack development intern between January and May 2026, in a work-study internship scheme (work for the company in the afternoons) for a total of 5 months.

# Role and activities
The main task entrusted to me was to design, replicate and modernise a SaaS platform for winegrowers to manage their stock and sales: VinoDomia. The old software had an outdated interface and significant maintenance limitations, as it was based on obsolete development tools. The strategic challenge was to completely rewrite the software as a web app using modern technologies, in order to provide simplified access from any device connected to the internet and to eliminate the need to install a resource-intensive programme on users’ machines. My work focused primarily on interface design, front-end architecture and the initial stages of back-end implementation.

During the first few days of the placement, I helped lay the groundwork for the project (creating the Git repository, setting up the necessary project dependencies and carrying out the necessary research to ensure the best possible start to the application’s development). Subsequently, over the following days, a planning phase was required with my internship supervisors to ensure we could start the project properly. It was decided that we would begin by modelling the various pages of the site, as well as the overlay that would allow us to navigate within the application, based on the numerous pages already present in the application, before moving on to their development. This part of the process, along with the implementation of responsive elements, took us a long time given the large number of pages and features in the original application. However, by using a UI library (Shuriken UI), development – particularly of certain parts of the front-end – was significantly accelerated thanks to the many pre-built functions and elements.\ n

For the development work, I mainly collaborated with another intern who was there at the same time as me, which meant we had to coordinate our work on the code.
Code reviews and approvals were carried out using a hybrid approach. We used instant messaging tools (Teams and Discord) for quick daily updates, 
supplemented by face-to-face meetings with our mentor to review our work before moving on to the next stages.\ n
# Curiosity, creativity & independence
Although I had completed several full-stack projects during my first two years of the Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science at Ynov, this immersive experience pushed me to demonstrate independence and creativity, particularly as I had to get to grips with a new framework (Nuxt/TypeScript), an ORM (Prisma) and a UI library (ShurikenUI) that I hadn’t yet explored in depth during my lectures, by carrying out my own research and keeping up to date with technical developments. When designing the numerous pages of the VinoDomia application, I took the initiative to improve the usability of the interfaces, proposing a more modern and intuitive design for winegrowers whilst adhering to the specifications.

# Personal assessment
## The student’s reflections on the experience gained:
This work placement was extremely rewarding. It enabled me to deepen my practical knowledge of full-stack development within a real professional environment, 
confirming my interest in designing robust software.\ n
## Professional development following the placement:
Apart from the skill enhancement on languages, libraries, and frameworks that were unknown to me, this experience has made me develop professionally. I have become more rigorous, particularly regarding code quality, managing deliverables and communicating within a development team. Furthermore, this placement enabled me to discover the basics of securing an authentication system using JWTs and role management, as well as the use of authentication-related middleware – components that are ubiquitous in modern web applications – which I was subsequently able to incorporate and utilise in numerous other projects throughout my second year at Ynov (e.g. for a mobile app featuring cookery recipes, for a Kanban-style organisation website, or for a website linked to a fictional estate agency for buying and selling properties). 

## Challenges encountered:
The need to master a new framework whilst immediately producing professional-quality, clean and maintainable code presented a complex challenge. This challenge nevertheless highlighted my ability to adapt and my perseverance. It did, however, reveal an initial need for closer supervision when getting to grips with unfamiliar tools – a weakness I was able to compensate for through my independent research and feedback from my internship supervisors.

Furthermore, having to completely redesign the pages of the old application also posed a significant challenge during the internship. This therefore required me to focus my efforts on the organisational work needed beforehand to provide a clean and user-friendly interface, whilst ensuring the page remained responsive.\ n
# Impact of the placement on my career plans 
Although web development is not necessarily my primary specialism for my future career, this placement has had a major impact on my career plans. It gave me a realistic insight into working methods in a professional environment and the rigour required in a company, and has equipped me with the technical versatility essential for approaching my future collaborations in the IT sector with confidence.



# *Glossary*
*SaaS*: ‘Software as a Service’ (SaaS), also known as ‘software on demand’, is a software delivery model in which software is installed on remote servers rather than on the user’s device. It is accessible via a subscription or freely online (e.g. Gmail, Notion, Slack, etc.). It enables businesses to fully outsource an aspect of their information system (e.g. email, security, etc.) and treat it as an operating cost rather than a capital expenditure.

*ORM*: An ORM (‘Object-Relational Mapping’) is a programming technique that creates a bridge between an application’s object-oriented code and a relational database.

*Git (Repository)*: A version control tool used by the development team to collaborate and centralise the project’s code.

*Framework*: A ‘framework’ in computer programming (also known as ‘software infrastructure’) is a set of pre-built software components in a particular language designed to facilitate or improve software development by imposing a basic architecture (e.g. Vue.js is a JavaScript/TypeScript framework). In contrast to libraries, frameworks provide an application’s skeleton and manage execution order.

*Tailwind CSS*: An open-source CSS framework built around utility classes, allowing developers to style HTML elements using those elements.

*Nuxt*: A framework working with the Vue.js ecosystem, which enables developers to create web applications with the help of server-side rendering mechanism.


*JWT* (JSON Web Token): An open standard (RFC 7519) that provides a compact and self-contained way for transmitting information between a client and a server. Used for accessing secure data from an API, because of the cryptographic signature.
